summary: A mail path — the missing capability three TKT-21 decisions were shaped around
description:
**As** a buyer who forgot their password, **I want** a way back into my account,
**so that** creating one is not a trap.

Filed after TKT-21 closed, because the epic kept running into the same wall. ADR-049 states it
plainly: *"This repo has no mail path. No SMTP, no queue, no provider. Every design that depends on
sending mail — email verification, password reset, 'we sent the owner a note' on a duplicate
registration — is unavailable, not merely unbuilt."*

**Three separate decisions were shaped by that absence, and two of them are worse than they need to
be:**

1. **Registration answers 409 on a duplicate** — an unauthenticated, unrate-limited membership oracle
   over the whole customer base (ADR-049 §2). The standard mitigation is *answer 201 and mail the
   owner*. **TKT-224** exists to rate-limit a disclosure that mail would remove outright.
2. **There is no password recovery of any kind.** `docs/development.md` § Customer accounts: *"A
   customer who forgets their password cannot get back in."* That is the largest hole in what TKT-21
   shipped, and it has no ticket until this one.
3. **No email verification**, so an account can register any address it does not own.

**This is a prerequisite, not a follow-up.** Two of the epic's three filed follow-ups exist to work
around it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] The service can send a transactional message, and **the plan states which service owns that
  capability and why** (ADR-002 cuts at five services; a mail sender belongs to one of them or the
  deviation is an ADR). Note that `access` already owns ticket *delivery* — say whether this is the
  same concern or a different one.
- [ ] A **local, offline sender** for `make up` and the smoke suite that captures messages instead of
  sending them — the gate must not depend on a network or a provider account, and a test must be able
  to assert what would have been sent.
- [ ] The plan states what happens when sending **fails**. A password reset that silently does not
  arrive is worse than one that refuses, and this is a queue-vs-inline decision with an ADR-016-shaped
  recovery question behind it.
- [ ] **Password reset** end to end: request, a single-use time-bounded token, set a new password,
  and every existing session for that customer invalidated (ADR-049 §4's session map is in-process —
  say how, or say it cannot and why that is acceptable).
- [ ] The reset flow does **not** reintroduce an enumeration oracle: requesting a reset for an
  unknown address answers the same as for a known one.
- [ ] The plan says whether TKT-224's **409 disclosure is now narrowed** (ADR-049 §2 becomes
  revisitable once mail exists) — decided either way, with the reason.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed BEFORE the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** marketing email, templates or branding · a provider integration beyond one port with
one fake (ADR-032's PSP-port shape is the precedent) · rate limiting (TKT-224) · GDPR retention of
message logs (TKT-33).

objective.note: A buyer who forgets their password can get back in, and the system can send a transactional message without a network.

scope.note: One sending port, one offline fake, one reset flow. Not templates, not marketing, not a provider account.

uncertainties.note: (a) which of the five services owns sending — access already owns ticket delivery, which may or may not be the same concern; (b) queue vs inline and what a send failure does; (c) whether reset invalidates in-process sessions or admits it cannot. All three are plan decisions with the constraints written down; none blocks starting.

dependencies.note: None. TKT-220..223 are Done and this depends on nothing they left open.

approach.note: Mirror ADR-032's PSP port: one interface, one fake used by make up and the smoke suite, one real implementation behind config. The fake is what makes the gate hermetic.

first_slice.note: The port plus the offline fake plus password reset. Verification and the 409 narrowing are separable and come after.

success.note: Deterministic: a captured message asserted by a test, a reset that works end to end, and an unknown-address request that is indistinguishable from a known one.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code before running the gate.

governingAdrs.why: States the absence this ticket closes, and the three decisions shaped around it: the 409 oracle (§2), no recovery path (Consequences), and the in-process session map (§4) that a reset would have to invalidate.
Five services. A mail sender lands inside one or the deviation is an ADR - and `access` already owns ticket DELIVERY, which is the closest existing concern.
The shape to copy: a provider behind a port with a fake, so the gate never needs a real account or a network.
A send that can fail and be retried is a recovery-state question, and this repo has an opinion about those.
Name the adversary. 'The reset link is single-use' means what, against whom - someone reading a mailbox, or someone with database access?

reference.summary: The disclosure this would let us close: ADR-049 §2 accepts registration's 409 as an unauthenticated membership oracle explicitly BECAUSE no mail path exists. TKT-224 is the mitigation built around it.
The operator-facing statement of the gap, already written: docs/development.md, 'There is no password recovery.'

### Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | OK | A buyer locked out of their own account can get back in |
| Scope | OK | One port, one fake, one reset flow |
| Uncertainties | WARN | Three, all deferred to plan time with their constraints written down |
| Dependencies | OK | None |
| AC verifiable | OK | Every criterion is a test or a stated decision |
| Context-mémo | OK | Baked, with the ADR-049 sections that constrain it |

**Concerns:**

1. **Ownership is genuinely undecided.** `access` owns ticket delivery today, which is either the
   same concern (one sender, two callers) or a different one (transactional identity mail is not
   fulfilment). Getting it wrong is a service-boundary mistake that costs a migration.
2. **This ticket makes TKT-224 partly redundant, and that is the point.** Rate limiting was designed
   around a disclosure mail removes. Whoever plans this should read TKT-224 first and say whether it
   shrinks.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable. Nothing structural; the uncertainties are decisions, not
unknowns.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-226

**Selection reason.** Chosen by the repo owner at Gate 1 over TKT-224/225/227. The TKT-21 handoff
recommended it and the reason holds: two of the epic's three filed follow-ups exist to work around
this absence, and one of them (TKT-224) is a control built on top of a disclosure that mail removes
outright. The largest product hole TKT-21 shipped — *a customer who forgets their password cannot get
back in* (`docs/development.md`) — has no other ticket.

**Blockers.** `links: []`. Zero open blockers. TKT-220…223 are Done and this depends on nothing they
left open.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** Stating it explicitly even though the answer is obvious,
because the label's carve-outs are exactly the tickets whose risk is obvious to the claimer and
invisible in the thread afterwards (TKT-190):

- **Auth path.** A password reset is a credential-change path. Getting the token single-use,
  time-bounded, and non-enumerating wrong is an account-takeover bug, not a defect.
- **Data migration.** A reset token needs storage; that is a commerce migration under ADR-022
  (out-of-band `migrate` subcommand), not an app-level change.
- **>5 files.** A port, a fake, a real-ish sender, a store, handlers, storefront pages, migration,
  compose wiring, and their tests. Nowhere near the threshold.
- **Session invalidation.** ADR-049 §4's session map is in-process. Invalidating every session for a
  customer crosses into that design, which the ticket names as an open decision.

Gate 2 therefore applies in principle. **This run is gateless by the owner's instruction** — I take
the gate decisions and every blocking objection I proceed past is recorded in the `overrides:` list
of the `kind=metrics` closeout. That list is the part an owner cannot reconstruct from the merged
diff.

**Branch.** `TKT-226-mail-path`, off `origin/main` @ `72a023d4`, in a worktrunk worktree.

**Deferred uncertainties carried into planning** (from `readiness.uncertainties`, all three are
decisions with their constraints written down, none blocks starting):
(a) which of the five services owns sending — `access` already owns ticket *delivery*;
(b) queue vs inline, and what a send failure does;
(c) whether reset invalidates in-process sessions, or admits it cannot and why that is acceptable.

Plus the ticket's own required call: **does TKT-224's 409 disclosure narrow now?** — decided either
way, with the reason.

### Execution plan — draft

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`** (codex companion, `task`, effort high, read-only — no repo file was modified). Config: `config.models.plan`. Codex session `019fd9ca-6310-7082-adba-3aeab0c324f7`.

Briefed by me from the ticket, the context-mémo, and a **claim-time re-resolution of the governing ADRs** — the mémo listed ADR-049/002/032/016/021; I added **ADR-043** (decides public-contract vs `/internal/` placement), **ADR-042**, **ADR-022** (the migration runs out-of-band) and **ADR-012** (a reset token is a bearer credential) before briefing.

---

# TKT-226 — execution plan

## 1. Decisions

### (a) Commerce owns transactional mail

`commerce` owns the mail port because it owns customer accounts, password credentials, reset tokens, and orders under ADR-002 and ADR-049. No sixth service, gateway-owned store, or cross-service NATS path is introduced.

`access` already owns ticket delivery attempts under ADR-012. That is a different concern: access delivers post-purchase ticket artifacts, while commerce sends account-lifecycle messages. The physical provider could eventually be shared, but ownership and retry state remain separate.

Create an ADR-050 documenting this boundary.

### (b) Use a durable transactional outbox, not inline sending

Password-reset token creation and mail-outbox insertion commit in one commerce transaction. A background mail drainer sends frozen message bytes after commit.

This follows ADR-016 §Decision 6 and the existing `services/commerce/internal/outbox/drainer.go` behavior:

- claim with a lease;
- send through the port;
- mark sent only after successful sender return;
- release with exponential backoff on failure;
- dead-letter after the existing bounded-attempt policy;
- never log the recipient, token, or message body.

If the database transaction or enqueue fails, the API returns a generic `503`; it does not claim that mail was accepted.

If sending fails after enqueue, the API’s prior `202` remains an honest “accepted for delivery” response. The row remains retryable and failures are operator-visible through persisted error state and logs. Exhaustion is dead-lettered rather than silently discarded.

No NATS routing is used, so ADR-017, ADR-033, and ADR-034 are not engaged.

### (c) Invalidate all sessions in the active storefront process

`commerce` cannot directly reach the storefront’s in-process `Map` from `web/storefront/src/lib/session.ts`.

The successful storefront reset route will:

1. receive the reset result, including `customer_id`;
2. call new `destroyAllSessionsForCustomer`;
3. delete the browser’s `SESSION_COOKIE`;
4. redirect to sign-in.

This invalidates every session for that customer in the current storefront process. Cross-replica invalidation remains impossible because ADR-049 deliberately chose process-local sessions; that limitation is acceptable for the current single-replica Compose topology and must be stated in ADR-050.

A direct caller of commerce’s public reset endpoint cannot invalidate a storefront map; the supported browser flow is the storefront route.

### (d) Narrow TKT-224’s registration disclosure after this ticket

Yes. Once mail exists, the duplicate-specific `409` should be removed in a follow-up.

Registration should return the same generic acceptance status and body for both a new and already-registered address, and should not return a principal. New accounts will require a subsequent sign-in. A duplicate attempt will queue an owner notification.

This removes the membership oracle that ADR-049 §2 accepted only because mail was unavailable. TKT-224 remains necessary for submission and mail-volume abuse; it is not replaced by this change.

## 2. The adversary, named

The reset token is a bearer credential.

It defends against:

- replay after successful use, through an atomic single-use update;
- replay after expiry, through a server-side expiry check;
- accidental exposure through gateway request logs, by carrying the token in an email URL fragment and submitting it later in a POST body;
- password-reset timing and response enumeration, through one generic response and the ADR-049 masked-cost discipline;
- network or browser observers who can see ordinary request URLs, because the fragment is not sent to the gateway.

It does not defend against:

- someone who can read the recipient’s mailbox;
- someone who can read commerce’s database, including the frozen mail-outbox payload;
- someone who can write commerce’s database or replace password/reset rows;
- a caller already inside the Compose network;
- cross-replica session invalidation.

The plan must not call this tamper-evident. It is an application-level recovery credential with bounded lifetime and use, not an integrity guarantee against a database adversary under ADR-021.

## 3. Definition of done

- Commerce exposes a provider-neutral mail port and deterministic offline fake.
- `make up` and smoke use the fake by default and perform no network mail calls.
- The fake captures complete messages for assertions.
- Migration `0018` creates reset-token and mail-outbox storage through ADR-022’s out-of-band `commerce-migrate` path.
- Reset request:
  - accepts an email;
  - returns the same status/body for known and unknown addresses;
  - never returns whether an account exists;
  - transactionally stores a hashed token and frozen mail message for known accounts.
- Reset completion:
  - accepts the token and new password in a POST body;
  - rejects malformed, expired, and previously used tokens;
  - updates the bcrypt password;
  - invalidates the token atomically;
  - returns the customer ID needed by the storefront to clear sessions.
- Existing storefront sessions for that customer are removed by `destroyAllSessionsForCustomer`.
- Reset pages and forms pass `gate.ts`’s proxy-aware origin check.
- Token values never appear in a gateway URL, response cache, application log, or rendered HTML.
- Existing account and guest-checkout paths remain unchanged.
- Generated `openapi_gen.go` and `commerce-api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and committed before `make check`.
- `make check` is green.
- A real browser submits both reset forms against `make up`; render-only verification is insufficient.

## 4. Files

### New

- `docs/adr/ADR-050-mail-path-and-password-recovery.md` — records mail ownership, outbox semantics, failure behavior, token threat model, and process-local session invalidation.
- `services/commerce/internal/mail/port.go` — new `Message` and `Sender` port.
- `services/commerce/internal/mail/fake.go` — offline capturing sender with deterministic failure injection.
- `services/commerce/internal/mail/fake_test.go` — proves capture behavior and no network dependency.
- `services/commerce/internal/mail/drainer.go` — mail outbox worker using the ADR-016 lease/retry/ack-before-mark protocol.
- `services/commerce/internal/mail/drainer_test.go` — pure drainer tests for success, retry, lease loss, and dead-letter behavior.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/password_reset.go` — reset-token creation/completion transactions, token hashing, and password update logic.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/mail_outbox.go` — Postgres claim, release, sent, and retry operations for mail rows.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/password_reset_test.go` — pure reset-token and validation tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/password_reset_smoke_test.go` — real-Postgres tests for transaction and driver behavior.
- `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/account/forgot-password.astro` — anonymous reset-request form.
- `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/account/reset-password.astro` — anonymous reset-completion form; reads the fragment locally and submits the token in the POST body.

### Modified

- `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` — declares public reset request/completion operations and schemas; quote all flow-mapping descriptions containing commas.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` — injects the sender, registers public reset routes, and starts the mail dependency wiring.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/customer.go` — preserves existing customer behavior while sharing generic error/no-store handling with reset handlers.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/password_reset.go` — new handlers for reset request/completion.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/password_reset_test.go` — handler mapping, response parity, no-reflection, and no-log tests.
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` — selects the fake sender by default and starts the mail drainer.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — regenerated and committed.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/commerce-api-types.gen.ts` — regenerated and committed.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/customer-api.ts` — adds reset request/completion calls using POST bodies and no-store behavior.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/session.ts` — adds `destroyAllSessionsForCustomer`.
- `web/storefront/test/session.test.ts` — tests customer-scoped invalidation.
- `web/storefront/test/gate.test.ts` — treats forgot/reset pages as anonymous and verifies unsafe submissions still require the trusted origin.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/locales.ts` — adds reset-page strings.
- `smoke/customer_accounts_test.go` — extends the existing live-commerce customer smoke seam with reset and fake-mail assertions.
- `compose.yaml` — makes the offline fake sender explicit for local Compose.
- `compose.smoke.yaml` — makes the offline fake sender explicit for smoke, if the override requires it.

The existing `services/commerce/internal/outbox/drainer.go` and `services/commerce/internal/store/store.go` remain the reference implementation for delivery semantics; the mail queue must not reuse `completion_outbox`, whose schema is order-event-specific.

## 5. The test seam

### Pure unit tests

Use dependency seams rather than real infrastructure for:

- `mail.Fake.Send`;
- mail message construction;
- reset token format and hashing;
- handler status/body mapping;
- reset-request response parity;
- logging and secret-reflection checks;
- `destroyAllSessionsForCustomer`;
- `gateRequest` classification and ordering.

The existing seams to preserve are:

- `customerStoreFn`;
- `compareCustomerHashAndPassword`;
- `registerCustomerFn`;
- `authenticateCustomerFn`;
- `lookupSession` and `next` instrumentation in `gate.test.ts`.

### Real Postgres tests

The fake-store learning requires real Postgres for anything involving:

- `INSERT ... RETURNING`;
- unique token-hash constraints;
- foreign keys;
- transaction atomicity;
- `UPDATE ... RETURNING`;
- `used_at` and expiry predicates;
- mail-outbox claim leases and retry columns;
- migration `0018`.

These belong in `services/commerce/internal/store/password_reset_smoke_test.go`, using the existing `outboxDB` and `schemaDB` helpers from the `store` package.

The real-Postgres tests must be written before relying on fake-store tests, because a fake cannot expose SQL driver behavior, constraint behavior, or the actual row scan.

### Browser submission

Against `make up`, submit:

1. `/en/account/forgot-password` with a known address;
2. the same form with an unknown address;
3. retrieve the captured fake message from the commerce database;
4. open the reset page using the fragment link;
5. submit the new password form;
6. verify the old password fails and the new password succeeds;
7. verify an existing browser session is redirected to sign-in after reset.

This must exercise Astro’s real form handling, relative actions, `gate.ts`, forwarded-origin headers, gateway routing, redirects, and cache headers.

## 6. Test plan

### Mail port and drainer

- `TestFakeSenderCapturesMessage` — fails if `Send` drops the message or mutates its recipient/body.
- `TestFakeSenderReturnsConfiguredFailure` — fails if configured failures are swallowed.
- `TestMailDrainerMarksSentOnlyAfterSend` — fails if the row is marked before sender success.
- `TestMailDrainerReleasesFailedMessageWithBackoff` — fails if a failed row disappears or is immediately retried.
- `TestMailDrainerDeadLettersAfterMaximumAttempts` — fails if poison mail retries forever or starves newer rows.
- `TestMailDrainerDoesNotLogRecipientOrToken` — fails if sensitive message data enters logs.

### Enumeration and request behavior

- `TestRequestPasswordResetAnswersIdenticallyForKnownAndUnknownAddresses` — fails if status or response bytes differ.
- `TestRequestPasswordResetComparesAtMaskedCostForKnownAndUnknownAddresses` — uses `compareCustomerHashAndPassword`; fails if the unknown path skips the fixed-cost comparison.
- `TestRequestPasswordResetDoesNotLogSubmittedAddress` — fails if the handler adds the email to outage logs.
- `TestResetRequestResponseIsNoStore` — fails if a reset response can be cached.

### Token lifecycle

- `TestPasswordResetTokenIsOpaqueAndNeverReturnedByTheStore` — fails if storage or return values expose the raw token.
- `TestCompletePasswordResetRejectsMalformedToken` — fails if malformed bearer input reaches a database lookup or produces a successful update.
- `TestCompletePasswordResetIsSingleUse` — fails if two completions succeed for one token.
- `TestCompletePasswordResetIsAtomicUnderConcurrentUse` — real Postgres; fails if concurrent requests both change the password.
- `TestCompletePasswordResetRejectsExpiredToken` — fails if expiry is checked using client time or after password mutation.
- `TestCompletePasswordResetUpdatesPassword` — fails if the new bcrypt credential is not the one accepted afterward.
- `TestResetTokenAndMailOutboxCommitTogether` — real Postgres; fails if either the token or its message can commit without the other.
- `TestPasswordResetMigration0018CreatesRequiredConstraints` — fails if migration numbering, foreign keys, uniqueness, or indexes are missing.

### Session invalidation

- `it('destroys every session for one customer and no other customer')` in `web/storefront/test/session.test.ts` — fails if one customer’s reset removes another customer’s sessions or leaves one of the target’s sessions alive.
- A storefront route test or browser check must fail if reset succeeds but the old session still reaches `/en/account`.

### Live smoke

Extend `smoke/customer_accounts_test.go` with:

- `TestPasswordResetIsReachableThroughTheGatewayWithoutACredential` — fails if the routes become internal or require a service token.
- `TestPasswordResetUnknownAndKnownRequestsHaveTheSameAnswer` — fails on response enumeration.
- `TestPasswordResetUsesTheOfflineCapturedSender` — fails if the outbox is not drained by the fake or if the captured message is absent.
- `TestPasswordResetCompletesThroughTheGateway` — fails if the message token cannot complete the reset, the old password still works, or the new password fails.

The smoke test must keep token/message values in memory and must not print them in failure output.

## 7. Risks

- **Token leakage through URLs:** putting the token in a query or path would expose it to gateway logs and traces. Use a fragment and POST body only.
- **Astro form rejection:** `make check` renders storefront pages but does not submit forms. Browser verification is mandatory.
- **Origin handling:** all reset POSTs must pass `web/storefront/src/lib/gate.ts`; do not restore Astro `checkOrigin`.
- **Outbox false success:** marking a mail row before `Sender.Send` returns would make a lost reset look delivered.
- **Dead-letter invisibility:** a failed sender must leave durable evidence and operator-visible logs without logging recipient or token data.
- **Fake-only confidence:** SQL constraints, transaction ordering, and scan types require real Postgres tests.
- **Session scope:** commerce cannot invalidate an arbitrary storefront process. The plan only claims invalidation in the active single-replica storefront process, matching ADR-049’s current session model.
- **Retention:** message rows may contain recipient data and frozen message content. GDPR retention and deletion remain TKT-33, not this ticket.
- **Generated drift:** run and commit `make generate` output before `make check`, per ADR-009.

## 8. Slicing

This should be split into two implementation tickets.

### TKT-226 first slice

- ADR-050;
- commerce mail port and fake;
- migration `0018`;
- durable mail outbox and drainer;
- password-reset request/completion API;
- storefront reset pages and session invalidation;
- real-Postgres, unit, smoke, and browser-submit verification.

### Follow-up ticket

- email verification;
- generic registration response;
- removal of the duplicate-registration `409`;
- owner notification for duplicate registration;
- storefront registration change from immediate session creation to subsequent sign-in;
- associated contract regeneration and browser-submit coverage.

No repository files were modified while preparing this plan.
